obligations.note: The new code in app.py match() handles GET /compat/account-number/<id> before the route table and builds an ad-hoc Route for the privileged action view_account_number with mfa=False. A privileged action is therefore served without MFA and outside the route table. The exhaustive routes control test only enumerates ROUTES, so its pass does not cover this path.
The register has no exception for MFA-1 on payments.http or payments.routes. The only MFA-1 entry (EXC-0172) is withdrawn and scoped to mortgage, so nothing excuses the deviation.
Ticket CHG-26510 is standard and approved by change manager Erik Brandt on 2026-10-04, before the change opened. Its components (payments.http) cover the only touched file, app.py.
The code_review approval is from Sofia Santos, a payments change_approver and a different person from the author Mara Costa.
Both approvals name head commit 74fd9836, which is the only commit on the change.

run.json names the head commit on ci-runner-01. The attached JUnit report, however, is stamped 2026-10-23 (after the 2026-10-08 review time) from host dev-laptop-7.local, so it cannot be tied to that CI run. Even if it were valid, the MFA control test does not reach the new bypass.
app.py is security_sensitive (payments.http). A security_review approval from Ines Halvorsen, a security_reviewer, is recorded on the head commit.
No protected paths are touched; the only changed file is apps/baseline-payments/payments/app.py.
The change is not an emergency (standard ticket, emergency=false), so no post-implementation review is due.
No acceptance-ledger entry covers app.py. ACR-0404 covers routes.py, which is unchanged, and MFA-1 is assessed on fresh grounds here anyway.

summary: PR-1249 adds a compatibility URL that match() serves before consulting the route table. It fabricates a route for the privileged view_account_number action with MFA disabled, so payee account numbers become retrievable without multi-factor authentication. This directly violates MFA-1, and no approved exception covers it. The CI JUnit evidence also does not match the recorded run (future timestamp, developer workstation host). Ticketing, independent code review and security review are in order, but the product control violation requires rejection.
